Diabetes supplies and the NDSS at Pacific Fair

Priceline Pharmacy Pacific Fair in Broadbeach is an access point for the National Diabetes Services Scheme (NDSS). If you’re registered, you can collect subsidised diabetes supplies from us and get advice from our pharmacists about managing your diabetes day to day.

Call (07) 5592 2099 Hours & directions

At a glance

What it is
Collection of subsidised NDSS supplies (test strips, pen needles, pump consumables, glucose monitoring products) and advice on managing diabetes.
Who it's for
People registered with the NDSS. The GPs at Help Medical can help you register.
Cost
NDSS subsidised prices apply.
Appointment
No appointment needed.
How to book
Show your NDSS card or number at the counter.

What is the NDSS?

The NDSS is an Australian Government initiative, administered by Diabetes Australia, that helps people with diabetes access subsidised products and support. You can learn more at ndss.com.au.

How do I register?

Registration needs a form signed by your doctor or credentialled diabetes educator. The GPs at Help Medical, an independent general practice located inside our store, can help. Once you’re registered, just show your NDSS card or number when you collect supplies.

Which supplies can I collect?

  • blood glucose test strips
  • urine and blood ketone test strips
  • pen needles and syringes
  • insulin pump consumables
  • continuous and flash glucose monitoring products, for eligible people

We stock products for all the major meter and monitoring brands, including Accu-Chek, FreeStyle, Contour and CareSens. If we don’t have your product on the shelf, we can order it in.

Medicines for diabetes, such as tablets and insulin, are prescription medicines and aren’t supplied through the NDSS. See prescriptions for how to send your script ahead.

How can our pharmacists support you?

  • setting up and using a new meter
  • storing insulin safely, including in Gold Coast summer heat
  • sick-day advice and what to do if your levels are out of range
  • checking interactions with other medicines
  • safe disposal of sharps

There’s no appointment needed. Ask at the counter, or call us on (07) 5592 2099 if you’d like to check we have your product in stock before you visit.

Not diagnosed but worried about type 2 diabetes?

Try a free AUSDRISK risk check at our Health Station. It’s a short questionnaire that estimates your risk of developing type 2 diabetes in the next five years, and our pharmacists can talk you through the result.

Common questions

What is the NDSS?

The National Diabetes Services Scheme is an Australian Government initiative, administered by Diabetes Australia, that helps people with diabetes access subsidised products and support.

How do I register for the NDSS?

Registration needs a form signed by your doctor or a credentialled diabetes educator. The GPs at Help Medical, inside our store, can help you with this.

What do I need to bring to collect NDSS supplies?

Just show your NDSS card or number at the counter. No appointment is needed.

What NDSS supplies can I collect at Pacific Fair?

Blood glucose test strips, urine and blood ketone test strips, pen needles and syringes, insulin pump consumables, and continuous and flash glucose monitoring products for eligible people.

Do you stock supplies for my meter?

We stock products for all the major meter and monitoring brands. If your product isn’t on the shelf, we can order it in.

Can I get my diabetes medicines through the NDSS?

No. Medicines for diabetes are prescription medicines, so bring or send us your prescription as usual. The NDSS covers supplies such as test strips and needles.

Can I check my risk of type 2 diabetes?

Yes. You can do a free AUSDRISK questionnaire at the Health Station inside our store, with a pharmacist nearby to talk through the result.
